You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Project System (PS).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Projects and WBS elements, networks/activities, project budgeting, time and expense posting to projects, settlement, results analysis.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Projects with WBS elements as costing objects; time and purchases postable to WBS; project cost report. Networks, scheduling, budgeting controls and settlement are not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the web search results, here's comprehensive information about SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) module capabilities:

## Overview

SAP S/4HANA Project System (PS) is a comprehensive solution for planning, executing, and controlling projects within the SAP S/4HANA ERP suite. The module supports various types of projects, including internal projects, customer projects, and capital investment projects.

## Key Capabilities

### Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
The module allows users to create and manage hierarchical project structures that define the tasks and deliverables of a project. A WBS allows mapping of a project structure using WBS elements found at different levels that structure the project based on a hierarchy.

### Networks
Network Activities enable users to define project tasks and relationships, including dependencies, durations, and resource assignments. Networks are used to map the flow of a project or parts of a project, with individual aspects mapped by activities linked by relationships.

### Budgeting and Cost Management
Budget Management capabilities include defining project budgets, monitoring actual costs against budgets, and enforcing budget controls to prevent overspending. Users can define and manage project budgets at the WBS level using CJ30 and cost planning, then release, supply, and return budgets.

### Settlement
The module provides an integrated framework for managing all project-related activities — from project initiation and budgeting to execution, costing, and final settlement — ensuring full transparency and control throughout the project lifecycle. Settlement is a periodic process where the costs and revenues collected on a project are "settled" to other controlling or financial objects. For customer projects, this is typically settled to a Profitability Segment in CO-PA to analyze the project's profitability.

### Additional Features
Cost Planning enables users to estimate project costs at various levels, such as WBS elements, network activities, or cost elements, and monitor actual costs against planned costs. Time and Labor Management captures and records employee time spent on project activities and calculates associated labor costs.

## Integration and Reporting
The system leverages the SAP HANA in-memory database to generate real-time project insights and facilitate faster decision-making.

## Project System Overview

Projects require precise planning of all associated activities, with project managers ensuring that projects are executed efficiently, on time, and within budget by ensuring that required resources and funds are available when needed.

## Project Structures

The Project System uses two structural approaches: a work breakdown structure (WBS) and individual activities (work packages). Projects are scheduled in the project planning board, and all editing transactions for work breakdown structures and networks can be executed in the Project Builder.

## Cost Planning

The WBS includes various planning methods such as hierarchy planning, unit costing, or cost element planning that can be used alternatively or together. Manual cost planning enables entry of expected costs, activities, and business processes for WBS elements, and can be used to compare planned costs and actual costs and analyze variances.

## Budget and Availability Control

Budget allocation for a project is generally preceded by a cost plan that provides the initial basis for determination and allocation of the budget. The funds overview is a passive availability control, where assigned funds are calculated and checked against the budget, and if tolerance thresholds are breached, this can trigger various system reactions such as warnings or error messages.

## CATS Time Sheet Integration

If activities are confirmed using CATS, the actual effort is updated in the cost collector in SAP S/4HANA and the tasks or project roles of SAP Project Management.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal PS documentation, SAP Community EPPM release blogs for S/4HANA Cloud 2502/2508, and SAP PRESS practitioner articles), supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge for structuring. S/4HANA Project System manages internal, capital-investment, and customer projects through hierarchical work breakdown structures (WBS) and optional networks/activities, covering structure planning, scheduling, cost and revenue planning, budgeting with availability control, execution postings (time via CATS, procurement, goods movements), and period-end close via settlement and results analysis / event-based revenue recognition. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026) the area spans classic PS (on-premise/private cloud) and the Fiori-based Enterprise Projects and Professional Services Projects in Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (public cloud), the latter pairing project control with event-based revenue recognition and milestone-linked billing. The Atlas v1 plan (WBS as costing objects, time and purchases postable to WBS, a project cost report) covers the execution-side core - structures and actual-cost collection - but deliberately omits the planning and financial-close layers: networks/scheduling, cost planning, budgeting/availability control, settlement, results analysis/revenue recognition, and customer-project billing are all out of scope for v1.

capabilities.description: Hierarchical project definition with WBS elements as account-assignment/costing objects, maintained via Project Builder or Fiori project apps with statuses and templates.
capabilities.later_path: Templates, status management, and mass-change tooling can be layered on the same WBS entity later.

capabilities.description: Task-level model beneath the WBS: activities with durations, work, relationships (dependencies), confirmations, and material components for logistics-driven projects.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 explicitly excludes networks; the v1 model is WBS-only cost collection with no activity/task layer.
capabilities.later_path: Add an activity entity under WBS elements with relationships and confirmations, then attach scheduling and material components.

capabilities.description: Forward/backward scheduling of dates across WBS and networks, project planning board (Gantt), critical path, and milestones that can trigger billing or workflows.
capabilities.reason: Scheduling is explicitly not in the v1 list and depends on the network/activity layer, which is also excluded.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce basic/forecast dates on WBS and activities plus a scheduling engine and Gantt view once networks exist.

capabilities.description: Planned costs per WBS element via hierarchy planning, cost-element planning, unit costing, or Easy Cost Planning, used as the baseline for budgets and variance analysis.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 collects only actual costs on WBS; no plan versions or planned-cost entry are in the plan, so the cost report has no plan/actual comparison.
capabilities.later_path: Add a plan-cost table keyed by WBS element and period, then extend the project cost report to plan-vs-actual.

capabilities.description: Original budget, releases, supplements/returns per WBS (CJ30 family) with active availability control that warns or blocks postings when assigned funds exceed tolerances.
capabilities.reason: Budgeting controls are explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 has no budget object and no posting-time funds check.
capabilities.later_path: Add a budget amount per WBS with tolerance rules evaluated in the posting pipeline before actuals commit.

capabilities.description: Employees record working time against WBS elements (or network activities) via timesheet; approved time posts labor cost to the project at an activity rate.
capabilities.later_path: Approval workflows and posting to network activities can follow once those features exist.

capabilities.capability: Procurement and expense postings to projects
capabilities.description: Purchase requisitions/orders, supplier invoices, goods movements, and journal entries account-assigned to WBS elements, including commitment tracking and project stock.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans actual purchase and expense postings to WBS, but PR/PO commitment tracking and project stock / project MRP are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Derive commitment records from open purchase orders assigned to WBS, then add project-stock segments in inventory.

capabilities.description: Period-end settlement of WBS costs to receivers - cost centers, assets under construction/fixed assets (investment projects), profitability segments (CO-PA) - via settlement rules.
capabilities.reason: Settlement is explicitly excluded from v1; collected costs remain on the WBS with no period-end transfer to receivers.
capabilities.later_path: Add settlement rules per WBS and a periodic settlement run reusing the finance allocation/posting engine.

capabilities.description: WIP calculation and POC-based revenue recognition for customer projects; classic results analysis in PS, or event-based revenue recognition with real-time Universal Journal postings in modern S/4HANA.
capabilities.reason: No revenue recognition or WIP/POC valuation of project costs is planned in v1; v1 projects are pure cost collectors.
